title: Square difference after a finite field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for $i=1,2,3$ be smooth separated morphisms of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] whose schemes are geometrically integral over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], meaning integral after every field extension. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Put $C=X_1\times_kX_2\times_kX_3$, $P=X_1\times_kX_1\times_kX_2\times_kX_2$, and let $\pi:P\times_kX_3\to P$ be projection. For an invertible module $A$ on $C$ [def-sc-invertible-module], write $r_{ab}:P\times_kX_3\to C$, $r_{ab}(x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1,z)=(x_a,y_b,z)$ for $a,b\in\{0,1\}$, and define its square difference on $P\times_kX_3$ by $$D(A)=r_{00}^*A\otimes r_{11}^*A\otimes(r_{01}^*A)^{-1}\otimes(r_{10}^*A)^{-1},$$ where inverse means the dual invertible module and all products, pullbacks and tensors are those of [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then there exist a finite field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-pc-field-tower], i.e. $[K:k]<\infty$, and an invertible module $N_K$ on $P_K=P\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$ such that, writing $A_K$ for the pullback of $A$ to $C_K=C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $D(A_K)$ for the same square difference formed over $K$ with the base-changed maps $(r_{ab})_K$, one has $D(A_K)\cong\pi_K^*N_K$ on $P_K\times_KX_{3,K}$.

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.2(ii), Claim 5.2.1 and the first paragraph of its proof, printed pp.11-12 (finite-extension square assertion); local copy WANTED.

proof.text: We will use the following geometry throughout, over $k$ and over any later field extension. Finite products of the factors are smooth by smooth base change and composition, and geometrically irreducible by the product theorem. Smooth geometric normality supplies geometric reducedness, so these products are geometrically integral and normal. They are locally Noetherian: on affine charts a finitely presented algebra over a field is finitely generated, hence the locally-finite-type Noetherian lemma applies. Each product projection used below is smooth, hence flat and locally of finite presentation; it is locally of finite type. Nonempty affine opens of the factors remain geometrically integral: their base changes are nonempty opens in integral schemes. Restrictions of smoothness to opens follow directly from its affine-local definition. Finite-type composition and base change give finite type for the products. Their diagonals are composites of base changes of the factor diagonals, hence are closed immersions; this verifies separatedness of $Z$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, smooth finite-presentation specialization; tensor rigidification and diagonal argument

proof.text: Apply the finite-closed-set rational-lifts lemma to the surjective morphism $X_1\amalg X_2\amalg X_3\to\operatorname{Spec}k\amalg\operatorname{Spec}k\amalg\operatorname{Spec}k$, with each factor mapped to its corresponding component and with the three points as the finite closed set. These schemes are finite type: the given finite-presentation maps are quasi-compact and have finitely generated affine coordinate algebras. The lemma gives one finite extension $K/k$ and points $x_*\in X_{1,K}(K)$, $y_*\in X_{2,K}(K)$ and $z_*\in X_{3,K}(K)$. Work over $K$ from now on and suppress its subscript. Choose affine neighbourhoods $U\subset X_1$ of $x_*$ and $V\subset X_2$ of $y_*$. They have the geometry checked in Step 1; affineness and the finite-presentation affine charts show finite type.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, smooth finite-presentation specialization; tensor rigidification and diagonal argument

proof.text: On $U\times_KV\times_KX_3$ restrict $A_K$ to $A'$ and form the invertible module $$B=A'\otimes a^*(A')^{-1}\otimes b^*(A')^{-1}\otimes c^*A',$$ where $a(x,y,z)=(x_*,y,z)$, $b(x,y,z)=(x,y_*,z)$, and $c(x,y,z)=(x_*,y_*,z)$. Pullback preserves tensor products and their invertibility. On $x=x_*$ the first two factors cancel and the last two cancel; on $y=y_*$ the first and third cancel and the second and fourth cancel. Thus $B$ is trivial on both coordinate slices. These are isomorphisms of invertible modules, obtained by reordering tensor factors and evaluation against their duals, rather than assertions about numerical classes.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, smooth finite-presentation specialization; tensor rigidification and diagonal argument

proof.text: Put $Z=X_3\times_KX_3$ and let $q_0,q_1:U\times_KV\times_KZ\to U\times_KV\times_KX_3$ select the first or second $X_3$ coordinate. Set $H=q_0^*B\otimes(q_1^*B)^{-1}$. The tensor identities and Step 3 make $H$ trivial on both $x=x_*$ and $y=y_*$. Step 1 gives that $Z$ is smooth separated finite type and geometrically integral. The clopen-locus lemma therefore applies to $(U,V,Z,H)$. The point $(z_*,z_*)$ lies in $E(H)$, since the two pulled-back factors agree there and cancel. An integral scheme is connected; a nonempty open and closed subset of a connected space is the whole space. Thus $E(H)=|Z|$, in particular the fibre of $H$ at the generic point of $Z$ is trivial.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, smooth finite-presentation specialization; tensor rigidification and diagonal argument

proof.text: Apply generic-line pullback descent to $f:U\times_KV\times_KZ\to Z$ and $H$. Step 1 supplies locally Noetherian source and target and normal integral target. The projection is flat and locally of finite type, and its fibres $(U\times_KV)_{\kappa(t)}$ are nonempty integral by geometric integrality. Step 4 supplies generic-fibre triviality. We obtain $H\cong f^*J$ for an invertible $J$ on $Z$. Pull back along $s:Z\to U\times_KV\times_KZ$, $s(t)=(x_*,y_*,t)$. Since $fs=\mathrm{id}_Z$ and $s^*H$ is trivial by the slice triviality, $J\cong\mathcal O_Z$. Consequently $H$ is trivial on the entire product.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, smooth finite-presentation specialization; tensor rigidification and diagonal argument

proof.text: Pull $H\cong\mathcal O$ back along $(x,y,z)\mapsto(x,y,z,z_*)$. If $B_*=B|_{U\times_KV\times\{z_*\}}$ and $p:U\times_KV\times_KX_3\to U\times_KV$, this says $B\otimes(p^*B_*)^{-1}\cong\mathcal O$, hence $B\cong p^*B_*$. On $Q=U\times_KU\times_KV\times_KV$ take the same four-term square as in the statement. Each correction $a^*A'$, $b^*A'$, $c^*A'$ in Step 3 omits $x$, $y$, or both. Its four square factors therefore cancel in pairs: for a factor independent of $x$, $r_{00}=r_{10}$ and $r_{11}=r_{01}$ on that factor, and for one independent of $y$, $r_{00}=r_{01}$ and $r_{11}=r_{10}$. It follows that $D(A_K)|_{Q\times_KX_3}\cong D(B)\cong\pi_Q^*D(B_*)$, where $D(B_*)$ is an invertible module on $Q$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, smooth finite-presentation specialization; tensor rigidification and diagonal argument

proof.text: The nonempty open $Q\subset P_K$ contains the generic point $\eta$ of the integral scheme $P_K$. Restricting Step 6 to the fibre over $\eta$ shows that $D(A_K)_\eta$ is pulled back from a one-dimensional $\kappa(\eta)$-vector space, hence is trivial after choosing a basis. Apply generic-line pullback descent again, now to $\pi_K:P_K\times_KX_{3,K}\to P_K$. Step 1 gives a normal integral locally Noetherian base and locally Noetherian source; this projection is flat and locally of finite type and every residue-field fibre is nonempty integral because $X_{3,K}$ is geometrically integral. The lemma gives an invertible module $N_K$ on all of $P_K$ and $D(A_K)\cong\pi_K^*N_K$, as required. The extension $K/k$ is the finite extension already constructed in Step 2.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, smooth finite-presentation specialization; tensor rigidification and diagonal argument
